# My Gujarat Property SaaS Rebuild — Requirement Traceability Matrix

## 1. Purpose

This document is the canonical traceability authority for the complete 47-file My Gujarat Property SaaS rebuild. It prevents any user instruction, Master UX obligation, constitutional rule, conflict decision, legacy-source requirement, terminology constraint, implementation obligation, verification obligation, or removal requirement from disappearing between documentation and production.

A requirement is not complete merely because it appears in a specification or a screen renders. Completion requires an unbroken chain:

```text
Source → atomic requirement → disposition → canonical owner → build phase → verification prompt → test → evidence → final result
```

No Claude agent, GitHub skill, reference website, implementation shortcut, existing code path, or visual artifact may bypass this chain.

## 2. Binding Traceability Rules

### MGP-TRACE-001 — Every non-informational source obligation receives a stable trace identifier.

### MGP-TRACE-002 — Compound source text is split into independently testable obligations without changing the preserved source.

### MGP-TRACE-003 — Removed or replaced requirements remain traceable and require negative evidence proving removal.

### MGP-TRACE-004 — A source-level mapping is not implementation completion; atomic behavior must be owned by a canonical specification.

### MGP-TRACE-005 — Every active requirement must map to at least one build phase and one verification/test path.

### MGP-TRACE-006 — Every visible action must map to a destination, state transition, permission, backend effect, feedback and recovery behavior.

### MGP-TRACE-007 — Every route/screen must map loading, empty, success, error, permission, refresh, Back and mobile behavior where applicable.

### MGP-TRACE-008 — Every removed feature must be checked across UI, routes, API, database, permissions, providers, notifications, analytics, tests and secrets.

### MGP-TRACE-009 — Every Master UX source line is covered through its section trace row and line manifest; section summaries may not weaken source wording.

### MGP-TRACE-010 — Every legacy heading is registered even when its content is removed, replaced, merged or deferred.

### MGP-TRACE-011 — GitHub skill execution is evidence only when the canonical requirement, resulting artifact, implementation and test are also present.

### MGP-TRACE-012 — Final File 47 may not be approved while any active material requirement lacks implementation and verification prompt coverage.

### MGP-TRACE-013 — Final File 45 sign-off fails if any material row is BLOCKED, UNMAPPED, UNTESTED or EVIDENCE_MISSING.

### MGP-TRACE-014 — Later user changes create new rows or versioned supersession links; prior evidence is never silently overwritten.

### MGP-TRACE-015 — Examples are global audit signals and cannot narrow the product to the example alone.

### MGP-TRACE-016 — The development server must remain running after successful final verification unless the user explicitly changes that rule.

### MGP-TRACE-017 — Trace status must reflect reality; documentation generation alone cannot set IMPLEMENTED or VERIFIED.

### MGP-TRACE-018 — Exact file paths and phase identifiers in this document must be reused by downstream files.

## 3. Requirement Lifecycle and Allowed Statuses

| Status | Meaning | May release? |
|---|---|---|
| `SOURCE_LOCKED` | Original source is preserved and integrity-checked. | No |
| `TRACE_REGISTERED` | Atomic or coverage row exists with owner, phase and test mapping. | No |
| `CANONICAL_SPECIFIED` | Owning canonical file contains complete behavior/data/permission/state rules. | No |
| `PLANNED` | File 47 contains a build prompt and a separate verification prompt. | No |
| `IMPLEMENTED` | Code, schema, configuration and migration changes are present. | No |
| `VERIFIED` | Required tests passed and evidence is linked. | Yes |
| `REMOVED_VERIFIED` | Prohibited feature is absent across all required layers with negative evidence. | Yes |
| `DEFERRED_APPROVED` | Explicitly deferred by canonical authority with no hidden partial implementation. | Only if launch-safe |
| `BLOCKED` | External dependency or unresolved material decision prevents honest completion. | No |
| `FAILED` | Implementation or verification failed. | No |
| `SUPERSEDED` | A later approved requirement replaces this row and links to the replacement. | No independently |

## 4. Mandatory Matrix Columns

| Column | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Trace ID | Unique immutable trace row. |
| Source anchor | Exact MGP-URV, MGP-UX, MGP-CONST, MGP-DEC, glossary or legacy-source identifier. |
| Atomic obligation | One testable requirement or explicit source-coverage obligation. |
| Disposition | KEEP, REMOVE, REPLACE, MODIFY, PROCESS, INFORMATIONAL, DEFER or SUPERSEDE. |
| Canonical owner | One or more exact file aliases from Section 5. |
| Build phase | One or more phase IDs from Section 6. |
| Verification/test family | Required automated/manual verification class. |
| Evidence | Required evidence artifact types. |
| Status | Lifecycle state from Section 3. |
| Result/notes | Final result, defect, supersession or approved limitation. |

File 47 must reuse these identifiers and provide both `BUILD-Pxx` and `VP-Pxx` blocks for every active phase.

## 7. Test Family and Evidence Registry

| Test family | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DOC` | File paths, contents, hashes, references and no-loss documentation checks. |
| `TRACE` | Source-to-spec-to-phase-to-test closure. |
| `SKILL` | Skill source audit, install/version proof and phase invocation. |
| `REPO` | Repository, route, component, schema and dependency audit. |
| `UX` | Orientation, task clarity, outcome and recovery. |
| `IA` | Information architecture and hierarchy. |
| `NAV` | Header/shell/menu/bottom-nav/breadcrumb/Back/Close behavior. |
| `ROUTE` | Direct URL, refresh, browser history and guard behavior. |
| `CONTAINER` | Page/modal/drawer/popover/sheet selection and behavior. |
| `AUTH` | Login, registration, onboarding and account-state behavior. |
| `OTP` | SMS OTP generation, expiry, resend, autofill, attempts and abuse controls. |
| `SESSION` | Session persistence, expiration, logout and reauthentication. |
| `REDIRECT` | Safe originating-context and role landing behavior. |
| `ROLE` | Role visibility, assignment and lifecycle. |
| `RLS` | Server-side authorization, scope and negative-access checks. |
| `HOME` | Homepage modules and contextual variants. |
| `SEARCH` | Query, suggestions, filters, sort, results, no-results and context preservation. |
| `NOTIFY` | Email delivery, homepage announcements and related navigation. |
| `PROPERTY` | Property lifecycle, public detail and dashboard management. |
| `PROJECT` | Project lifecycle, public detail and builder management. |
| `UNIT` | Nested Project Unit behavior. |
| `INQUIRY` | Direct Inquiry flow and duplicate control. |
| `LEAD` | Lead creation, context, status, history and permissions. |
| `CONTACT` | Phone visibility and anti-scraping policy. |
| `BANNER` | Builder banner eligibility, payment, targeting, lifecycle and analytics. |
| `BILLING` | Plan, trial, subscription, invoice, tax, payment and webhook behavior. |
| `ADMIN` | Admin/Super Admin entity graph and operations. |
| `MOD` | Moderation state machine, decisions, correction and recovery. |
| `AUDIT` | Immutable actor/action/time/before/after history. |
| `CMS` | Content management and publishing. |
| `SEO` | Indexable pages, metadata, canonical and structured data. |
| `LEGAL` | Terms, privacy, consent and disclaimers. |
| `SUPPORT` | Support/reporting/abuse workflows. |
| `FORM` | Validation, submission, unsaved changes and server errors. |
| `STATE` | Loading, empty, success, failure, disabled and processing states. |
| `ERROR` | Error boundaries, recovery and contextual fallback. |
| `RESP` | Mobile/tablet/desktop and intermediate-width behavior. |
| `A11Y` | Keyboard, focus, semantics, labels, touch targets and assistive technology. |
| `CONTENT` | Wrapping, clipping, localization resilience and long data. |
| `DB` | Schema, constraints, indexes and durable data. |
| `API` | Service contract, validation, idempotency and errors. |
| `MIGRATION` | Safe legacy transformation, rollback and verification. |
| `STORAGE` | Media upload, compression, delivery and access. |
| `SEC` | Threat controls, secrets, abuse, privacy and scanning. |
| `PERF` | Latency, caching, query efficiency and resource budgets. |
| `LOAD` | Capacity and staged concurrency testing. |
| `OBS` | Logs, metrics, traces, alerts and operational dashboards. |
| `DR` | Backup, restore, failover and disaster recovery. |
| `DEPLOY` | CI/CD, environment promotion and production checks. |
| `ROLLBACK` | Application/database rollback and recovery drill. |
| `SERVER` | Project run/health and final server-running evidence. |
| `E2E` | Complete real user journeys. |
| `NEGATIVE` | Denied, invalid, failure and abuse journeys. |
| `REMOVAL` | Cross-layer proof that prohibited functionality is gone. |
| `PROMPT` | Final Claude prompt completeness and executability. |

Evidence must use concrete artifacts such as command logs, migration output, screenshots, screen recordings, network captures, database rows, email captures, audit events, load reports, security scan reports, accessibility reports, monitoring dashboards and restore drills. A prose claim is not sufficient evidence.

## 19. Final Prompt File Coverage Contract

File 47 must:
- read Files 1–46 in authority order before implementation;
- verify source hashes and repository state before modifying code;
- install or validate phase-relevant GitHub skills safely and record versions/commits;
- provide one `BUILD-Pxx` prompt and one separate `VP-Pxx` verification prompt for every phase P00–P17;
- name the exact canonical files each phase must read;
- name the exact features, routes, data entities, migrations, permissions, states and tests the phase owns;
- run the real project during verification;
- fix failures and repeat verification instead of reporting a false PASS;
- collect evidence using File 46;
- update this matrix from TRACE_REGISTERED through VERIFIED/REMOVED_VERIFIED;
- perform a final zero-unmapped, zero-unimplemented, zero-untested and zero-evidence-missing audit;
- keep the verified development server running at completion;

## 20. Matrix Update Procedure

1. When a canonical spec is generated, update its owned rows to CANONICAL_SPECIFIED only after all behavior, state, data, permission and failure requirements are present.
2. When File 47 creates the implementation and verification pair, update rows to PLANNED.
3. After code/schema/configuration is implemented, update to IMPLEMENTED and add changed-file/migration references.
4. After tests pass, attach evidence references and update to VERIFIED or REMOVED_VERIFIED.
5. If a test fails, set FAILED; do not leave the row at IMPLEMENTED.
6. If an external provider or user decision blocks completion, set BLOCKED and record exact dependency; never claim PASS.
7. When a later user instruction changes scope, add a superseding row and cross-link the old row as SUPERSEDED.
8. Before release, File 45 must calculate counts by status and reject release for any disallowed status.
